page: Microsoft Azure D48als_v6 belongs to the Dalv6 server family, powered by a 64-bit AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. The instance provisions 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. Hardware acceleration flags include AVX-512 extensions (such as VNNI and BF16) and standard cryptographic instructions including AES and SHA-NI. The host runs on Microsoft Hyper-V and supplies 96.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no integrated local storage and contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight strong compute capabilities, with top-quartile execution scores in stress-ng multi-core testing at 73,831.66 and Geekbench multi-core at 20,465.0. Instruction-dense tasks reflect high efficiency, registering strong marks in Clang compilation (46,871.0) and ray tracing (60,113.0). Uncached large-block memory bandwidth tests measure 113.41 GB/s for reads and 82.27 GB/s for writes. In application benchmarks, the server delivers high throughput with 66.68 million Redis SET operations per second and fast prompt evaluation on smaller language models, though large 70B parameter models show constrained text generation throughput.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio represents a core-dense hardware profile, prioritizing raw computing capacity over expansive memory footprints. Because no onboard NVMe or SSD storage is bundled, all persistence relies on networked remote storage attachments. This resource balance provides high qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks where large RAM arrays are unnecessary, making the instance well suited for continuous integration build clusters, multi-threaded batch jobs, backend web serving, and high-throughput key-value caching.
description: Microsoft Azure D48als_v6 is a compute-focused general-purpose instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the system includes 96.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) without bundled local storage or discrete GPUs. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates AVX-512 vector extensions and cryptographic accelerators, driving top-quartile multi-core benchmark results in stress-ng, Geekbench, and Clang compilation tests. It delivers high transactional rates, achieving 66.68 million Redis SET operations per second alongside balanced large-block memory bandwidth. With persistent storage requiring network-attached disks, the instance provides cost-effective density for compute-intensive workloads that do not demand expansive memory footprints. The D48als_v6 is well suited for parallel compilation, distributed batch processing, backend microservices, and medium-scale in-memory caching layers.
